layers.basics: Iron cores guide magnetic flux like wires guide current, with turns×current acting as the push (mmf).
layers.deeper: Reluctance ℜ=ℓ/μA; air gaps dominate reluctance; saturation limits flux density near 1.5–2 T for silicon steel.
layers.expert: Core loss = hysteresis + eddy (laminations cut eddy); B–H curves; fringing; inductance L=N²/ℜ.

layers.basics: Power transformers step voltage up for transmission and down for use; efficiency exceeds 99%.
layers.deeper: Equivalent circuit: winding resistance, leakage reactance, magnetising branch; tests: open- and short-circuit.
layers.expert: Voltage regulation, per-unit impedance, three-phase connections (Δ–Y); inrush current; cooling classes (ONAN); losses ∝ I² and core loss ∝ B².

title: DC machines

layers.basics: A DC motor’s coil in a magnetic field feels torque; a commutator flips current to keep it turning.
layers.deeper: Torque ∝ flux × armature current; speed ∝ V/flux; brushless DC replaces the mechanical commutator with electronics.
layers.expert: T=k_tΦI_a, E_b=k_eΦω; speed control by armature voltage or field weakening; separately excited, series and shunt types.

formula: T = k_t I,  E_b = k_e ω

layers.basics: Three-phase currents create a rotating magnetic field; it drags a rotor around by induced currents.
layers.deeper: The rotor lags the field by a slip s of a few percent; no brushes needed.
layers.expert: N_s=120f/P; torque–slip curve with peak at s_max; equivalent circuit; V/f control for variable speed.

layers.basics: A synchronous machine’s rotor turns exactly in step with the grid frequency; most power plants use huge ones as generators.
layers.deeper: Excitation current controls reactive power; load angle controls real power.
layers.expert: Power–angle P=(E V/X_s)sinδ; stability limit at 90°; permanent-magnet synchronous motors common in EVs.

title: Generation of electric power
summary: Turning fuel into spin into electricity.

layers.basics: Steam, gas, water or wind turn turbines that spin generators; solar panels make DC directly.
layers.deeper: Base-load, peaking and variable plants; efficiency limited by heat-engine (Carnot) theory for thermal plants.
layers.expert: Combined-cycle gas ~60% efficient; hydro >90%; capacity factor; inertia from rotating mass stabilises frequency.

layers.basics: High voltage cuts current for the same power, so wires lose less as heat; substations step voltage down near users.
layers.deeper: Typical levels: 765/345/230 kV transmission, 11–35 kV distribution, 120/230 V utilisation.
layers.expert: Line losses I²R; surge-impedance loading; long lines need reactive compensation; HVDC beats AC beyond ~600 km overhead.

layers.basics: Expressing voltages, currents and impedances as fractions of chosen base values simplifies calculations across transformers.
layers.expert: Per-unit transformer impedance is the same on both sides; change of base Z_pu,new=Z_pu,old(S_new/S_old)(V_old/V_new)².

title: Power flow analysis
summary: Solving for voltages and flows in a grid.

layers.basics: Power-flow studies compute bus voltages and line flows for given generation and load, using iterative solvers.
layers.deeper: Gauss–Seidel, Newton–Raphson; bus types: slack, PV, PQ.
layers.expert: Y_bus matrix; NR Jacobian; DC power flow approximation P=Bθ; optimal power flow adds cost minimisation.

title: Fault analysis
summary: What happens in a short circuit.

layers.basics: A fault creates huge currents; analysis predicts them so equipment can be sized and protected.
layers.deeper: Faults: three-phase, line-to-ground, line-to-line; symmetrical components simplify unbalanced faults.
layers.expert: Zero, positive and negative sequence networks; fault current I_f=V/Z_th; breaker interrupting rating and X/R ratio.

title: Protection: relays and circuit breakers
summary: Cutting the power safely and fast.

layers.basics: Relays sense abnormal currents and trip breakers that interrupt them within a few cycles.
layers.deeper: Overcurrent, differential and distance relays; breakers quench the arc with SF₆, vacuum, or air.
layers.expert: Coordination curves; zones of protection; arc extinction at current zero in AC; DC breakers are harder (no zero crossing).

title: Power grid, renewables and smart grid

layers.basics: Supply and demand must match every instant; wind and solar vary, so storage, flexible demand and communication help.
layers.deeper: Inverters feed solar into the grid; grid-forming inverters replace the inertia of spinning generators; smart meters enable demand response.
layers.expert: Frequency control (primary, secondary), RoCoF, duck curve; synchrophasor measurement; microgrids; cybersecurity of grid control.

open_questions: How to keep inertia-free grids stable at very high renewable share?
What storage mix is cheapest for multi-day lulls?

layers.basics: Controlled rectifiers convert AC to adjustable DC; inverters create AC from DC using fast switches and PWM.
layers.deeper: H-bridge with sine-weighted PWM; three-phase inverters drive motors and feed solar into the grid.
layers.expert: SPWM, space-vector modulation, THD; thyristor phase control; active front end and PFC; DC-link capacitors.

layers.basics: A switch chops the input and an inductor–capacitor filter averages it, giving a lower output with little loss.
layers.deeper: V_out=D·V_in in continuous conduction; ripple from L and C.
layers.expert: ΔI_L=(V_in−V_out)D T/L; CCM/DCM boundary; synchronous rectification; control by voltage-mode or current-mode.

title: Boost and buck-boost converters
summary: Step up, or step up and down.

layers.basics: Boost: output above input. Buck-boost: output of either size, inverted.
layers.deeper: Boost V_out=V_in/(1−D); inductor stores energy while the switch is on and releases it through a diode.
layers.expert: RHP zero in boost control loop; flyback derived from buck-boost with a coupled inductor; efficiency 85–98%.

layers.basics: Switch-mode supplies chop DC at 50 kHz–2 MHz through small transformers and inductors, replacing bulky 50/60 Hz parts.
layers.deeper: Topologies: flyback, forward, half/full bridge, LLC; isolation via transformer and optocoupler or secondary-side control.
layers.expert: Magnetics design (area product); snubbers; EMI filters; soft switching (ZVS) improves efficiency; GaN enables MHz operation.

layers.basics: A drive turns fixed mains into variable-frequency variable-voltage power, so motors run at any speed efficiently.
layers.deeper: V/f control for simple loads; field-oriented control for high performance.
layers.expert: FOC decouples torque and flux through Clarke/Park transforms; encoders or sensorless estimation; regenerative braking.

layers.basics: Power MOSFETs, IGBTs and wide-band-gap SiC and GaN devices handle high voltage and current with low loss.
layers.deeper: IGBT: MOS gate with BJT conduction for 600 V–6.5 kV; SiC MOSFET and GaN HEMT switch faster with lower loss.
layers.expert: Wide band gap raises breakdown field (SiC 2.8 MV/cm vs Si 0.3), allowing thinner drift layers; figure of merit R_on·Q_g; thermal limits and packaging.
